definition: How fast a reaction goes: the increase in a product's concentration, or the decrease in a reactant's, per unit time, usually in mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. It is always a positive value.
The model that particles react only when they collide, and only if the collision has at least the activation energy and the proper orientation.
A collision between reactant particles with energy equal to or greater than the activation energy and the proper orientation, so that they react.
A straight line that touches a curve at one point and has the same gradient there. On a concentration–time graph its gradient gives the rate at that time.
